rule/seq: A model reads the letters K, D, R, A, M, and then K again. What comes next?
rule/guess: Text repeats, so a good guess is D: the last time K appeared, D came right after it. Seen K D before, now K: predict D.
rule/two: Trained models learn this rule with two attention heads working one after the other. The second is called an induction head.
prev/back: In an earlier layer, a previous-token head attends one position back, at every position.
prev/write: It writes what it finds into the stream. So position one, the D, now carries a note: my previous token was K.
match/query: In a later layer, at the second K, the induction head's query looks for a key that says: my previous token was K.
match/hit: Only position one matches, so the head attends there, to the D. The causal mask allows it: the D is in the past.
match/copy: It copies D into the current stream, raising the score of D as the next token. Neither head helps alone, but together they continue any pattern the text has already shown.
